Direct HTTP proves single-use password refresh and prior access expiry; rotation preserves existing password/API bearers and password refresh. Repeated client_credentials is verified, but timed automatic credential renewal and two-hour expiry are not waited out.
Adapter refresh replay remains intentionally stricter than the observed Vaultwarden1.37.4 baseline. Exact OAuth error envelopes and complete response metadata remain partial.

Device discovery has a separate opt-in DeviceStorage registry and typed read services. The adapter login savepoint atomically registers verified owner/device metadata with token/session binding, while refresh preserves the bound identifier and failed credentials create no device. Original name/type/creation and account revision are preserved on repeat login. Separate session-targeted push-token and authentication-request creation/discovery/approval/polling services have partial contracts. A personal auth-request password-grant variant now consumes an approved request before registering its newly supplied form device and issuing password authority. Enabled relay, complete account-verification/2FA/SSO variants and broader device policy remain open.

Additional reusable service: auth_login::VaultService::authenticate_auth_request in crates/no-warden/src/auth_login.rs:163 validates AuthRequestLoginRequest and returns private-constructor AuthorizedAuthRequestGrant owning the provider OwnerId without core allocation or provider-borrow retention. AuthRequestLoginRecord/Context/device/grant Debug output is redacted; the record and grant are internal, not serializable OAuth responses. The primary service reference stays authenticate_api_key because both variants share one routed pattern.

Pinned identity.rs370-498 and AuthMethod::check_scope require grant_type=password, scope exactly api offline_access, and present client_id/password/username/deviceIdentifier/deviceName/deviceType. authRequest must be present to select this variant; its case-insensitive compact Rocket name root also matches dotted/bracketed forms such as authRequest.x, authRequest[x], .aUtHrEqUeSt and [authRequest], with no auth_request underscore alias. All recognized roots select request-code verification rather than ordinary password fallback. The core separately requires auth_request presence. Present empty client/device/code strings remain distinguishable from missing fields. Adapter form aliases preserve source compact/underscore variants for their applicable fields; duplicate or ambiguous decoded aliases retain the adapter's stricter rejection policy.

Username is trimmed with Rust str::trim before provider Unicode lowercase lookup. Password carries the exact request access code, replacing account-password verification for this branch; account master hashes and the approved request's masterPasswordHash/key are not login proofs. Empty/malformed/unknown present authRequest values fail this branch rather than falling back to ordinary password verification. The form request ID is an opaque exact string, with no URL UUID guard or canonicalization.

Core checks exact owned request ID, approved=Some(true), unused state, authoritative provider account_enabled, exact trusted request IP and now<creation plus 300 seconds. The checked i128 nanosecond deadline rejects the exact boundary and arithmetic overflow; future creation timestamps are not rejected merely for being future, matching source comparison. Login deliberately does not compare new form device identifier/type with the requesting device. The HTTP suite authors a real 301-second wait without a clock override; precise nanosecond/future/overflow/disabled variants use core and host provider tests, not portable HTTP claims.

AuthRequestLoginStorage::auth_request_login performs constant-time code verification; consume_auth_request_login atomically compares owner/ID/approved/unused and records the authentication timestamp before any AuthorizedAuthRequestGrant is returned. The host mutex and outer savepoint cover consume, device registration/activity, access/refresh sessions and session-device binding, rolling all back on late failure. This adapter failure guarantee is stronger than pinned upstream issuance timing. Private CAS/concurrency/rollback/reopen/disabled behavior uses host SQL tests; public projection equality does not prove hidden state or database atomicity.

The grant carries password-method scope api offline_access and refresh permission, preserving the requested client ID and raw new device metadata. Shared non-API issuance now uses 7200-second access authority; refresh accepts a replacement client_id and defaults missing client ID to undefined, preserving bound device identity. Auth-request login responses return the account's existing Key/PrivateKey, never substitute the approved request's opaque key/hash. Existing stricter single-use refresh replay policy and complete OAuth envelope differences remain partial; a two-hour real expiry wait is not claimed.

The eight authored --suite auth-login cases include 43 identity requests (two ordinary logins, seven successful request logins, two refreshes and 32 rejections) and 24 public attempts (12 creates/12 polls), with at most 10 token and five public requests per direct loopback peer under unchanged reference defaults. Four additional case 7 dotted/bracketed authRequest root negatives use separate peers 30-33. No forwarding-header spoofing, retries or clock override is used. Auth-request consumption blocks login replay but leaves stored approval/key/hash and public response polling readable; creation expiry only blocks login, not the separate public polling endpoint. Both the standalone adapter and actual Vaultwarden1.37.4 passed all eight cases with 444 counted HTTP requests each and exit 0. The real creation-expiry scenario observed an age of 301 seconds. No 429/rate, configured trusted-forwarding, actual CLI auth-request flow or formal exhaustive parity claim is made.

Concrete private-state tests: store.rs auth_login_exact_nanosecond_deadline_and_private_policy_are_authoritative, auth_login_bad_proofs_owner_ip_pending_used_and_cas_do_not_mutate, auth_login_consumption_reopens_and_concurrent_cas_has_one_winner; main.rs auth_login_late_failures_roll_back_consumption_activity_sessions_and_bindings and auth_login_replay_race_issues_exactly_one_bound_session. Their SQL/host fault-injection authority is separate from portable HTTP snapshots.

Nested authentication/unlock KDFs compare every signed/optional field before normalization; both salts must exactly equal raw email.trim().to_lowercase().

The provider verifies token signature, exact configured purpose issuer and NumericDate validity before returning an owned claims handle.
